workflows.name: Send daily Proxmox VE health reports to any webhook

user.name: Pontavia Consulting
user.bio: Proxmox and n8n automations by Mike Maiolo, Pontavia Consulting. Read-only by default, tested on real clusters.

workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow runs daily or on demand to read Proxmox VE cluster health (nodes, storages, backups, snapshots, and recent tasks), grades findings as OK/WARNING/CRITICAL, optionally posts a single alert to a configurable webhook endpoint, and returns the full report.

How it works
Runs every morning at 7am on a schedule or when you POST to the manual webhook endpoint.
Calls the Proxmox VE API to fetch cluster resources (nodes, guests, storages), guests not covered by any backup job, and recent cluster tasks.
Filters for available backup storages and queries the Proxmox VE API for each storage’s backup file listing.
Filters for non-template guests (excluding any configured IDs) and queries the Proxmox VE API for each guest’s snapshot list.
Combines all retrieved data into a single health report, grading issues like offline nodes/storages, low backup coverage, stale backups, old snapshots, and failed tasks.
Posts the report to the configured alert webhook when the status meets your alert threshold (or when forced to alert on OK).
Fails the execution if any Proxmox data could not be read; otherwise returns the report JSON as the workflow output.

Setup
Create a Proxmox VE user and API token with read-only permissions sufficient for cluster, VM/CT, backup, and datastore audit (and datastore allocate space if required to list backup files).
In n8n, create an HTTP Header Auth credential with header name Authorization and a PVEAPIToken=... value, and select it on all Proxmox HTTP Request nodes.
In “Set Configuration Parameters”, set api_url to your Proxmox API base URL and configure thresholds like backup_max_age_hours, snapshot_max_age_days, and storage warning/critical percentages.
Set alert_url to your target webhook (or leave it blank to disable alerts) and adjust alert_on/alert_when_ok to control when notifications are sent.
If using the manual run, copy the “Run Now Webhook” URL and send a POST request to test end-to-end connectivity and output.

Free sampler of our agent skills: https://solokit33.gumroad.com/l/agent-skills-sampler

workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow receives an agent’s final reply and tool execution log via webhook, checks whether the reply claims actions that aren’t supported by completed tool results, optionally posts gaps to Slack via an Incoming Webhook, and logs every check to Google Sheets.

How it works
Receives a POST request on the /webhook/say-do-check webhook containing an agent reply plus either a tool-call log or an n8n execution JSON with a node map.
Applies your configured failure markers and node mapping to normalize tool-call results and infer whether each action actually finished.
Extracts completed-action claims from the reply text (and optionally from a structured actions array) and grades each claim against the tool-call evidence.
Produces a verdict of pass, review, or stop_ship and returns it to the caller along with findings, duplicates, gap counts, and a text report.
If configured to notify (gaps, stop-ship only, or always), posts a formatted review message to Slack using the Slack Incoming Webhook URL.
Appends a row to Google Sheets with the verdict, gap metrics, reply text, and report for audit and tracking.

Setup
Set the Slack Incoming Webhook URL, Google Sheets spreadsheet ID, and target sheet tab name in the Config step.
Connect Google Sheets OAuth credentials for the Google Sheets append action.
Create the header row in your sheet tab: timestamp, receivedAt, source, verdict, stopShip, claims, gaps, gapRate, reply, report.
If you plan to send n8n execution JSON instead of a raw tool log, update the default node map in Config to match your workflow’s reply node and action nodes.
Activate the workflow, copy the production webhook URL for /say-do-check, and configure your agent/calling workflow to POST the reply plus tool log (or execution + node map) to it.

Requirements
Slack workspace (Incoming Webhook) and Google Sheets. No AI key. No community nodes.

Customization
Edit notifyOn in Config: gaps (any unsupported claim), stop_ship (only pay or delete gaps), or always. Change defaultNodeMap to match your agent workflow (reply node name and field, plus each action node with action, id path, and target path or target_value). Edit failureMarkers to match your APIs; an empty list turns off body checks, while HTTP 4xx or 5xx and a failed status string still count. Swap Slack for email if you prefer.

Additional info
A buyer can put this in front of any send step and hold a message when the agent claimed "I refunded the order" or "all set" but the refund node timed out or never ran. The check is deterministic (verb, target, amount and evidence grade, including a hard stop-ship on pay or delete), needs no AI key, and returns a verdict the calling workflow can branch on.

Limitations:
This checks a finished reply. It does not recall a message that already went out. Run it before you send.
Targets are only as good as the tool log or node map. n8n often does not store a resolved recipient, so target_value is sometimes a fixed string.
Only the first output item of each node run is read.
Replies with no completed action claims pass, including future tense such as "I will send it", unless a structured actions list is present.
The verb list still misses some phrasings. Version 1.2.0 covers the passive and noun cases listed above; unusual wording can still pass quietly unless you send a structured actions array.
Anyone who can POST to the webhook can run a check. Keep the URL private or put the workflow behind authentication.
An invalid payload (missing reply, or no calls and no execution) stops the run with an error before a webhook response is sent.
If Slack or Sheets fails after the verdict has already been returned, the caller still has the JSON result but the notify or log step may be missing.
No duplicate check across requests. The same payload posted twice is checked twice.
Unusual API bodies may need the failureMarkers list in Config edited. An empty list turns off body checks.

workflows.name: Log weekly Google Ads Transparency creatives to Google Sheets with Apify alerts via Slack or email
workflows.description:
Quick overview
Each week this workflow runs the Google Ads Transparency Scraper Actor on Apify for a list of advertiser names or domains, appends only new creatives to a Google Sheet, and sends a Slack or email alert when something new appears after the first baseline run.

How it works
Runs on a Monday weekly schedule (or manually for testing) and loads configuration such as advertiser queries, region/format filters, and notification settings.
Calls the Apify Google Ads Transparency Scraper Actor with the configured queries and limits, and retrieves the resulting dataset.
Filters the Apify dataset to keep only rows that represent ads and include a creativeId.
Reads existing rows from the target Google Sheets tab and compares creativeId values to detect creatives not already logged.
Appends any newly found creatives to Google Sheets with metadata like advertiser, dates shown, URLs, and timestamps.
If this is not the baseline run and new creatives were added, sends a digest alert to either Slack or email based on your notifyVia setting.

Setup
Install the verified community node @apify/n8n-nodes-apify (n8n 1.57.0 or later). On n8n Cloud, the instance owner may need to allow verified community nodes. See https://docs.apify.com/integrations/n8n
Connect an Apify API credential (API token from Apify Console → Settings → Integrations / API). Do not paste tokens into the workflow.
Connect Google Sheets, plus Slack or SMTP, matching notifyVia in the configuration node.
In Configure weekly check, set queries (one advertiser name or domain per line), region, format, maxAdsPerAdvertiser, notifyVia (slack or email), and the Google Sheet ID.
Create a Google Sheet whose first row is: creativeId, advertiserName, advertiserId, format, firstShown, lastShown, daysShown, adUrl, query, region, imageUrl, previewUrl, scrapedAt, loggedAt. Use the sheet name in the configuration node (default Ad creatives).
Run the workflow once with the manual trigger to build the baseline, then enable the Monday schedule. Alerts for new creatives start on later runs.

Requirements
Required package: @apify/n8n-nodes-apify (tested with 0.9.0 on n8n 2.47.7)

Additional info
List price is $0.0015 per ad saved on the Apify Free plan; paid plans are slightly lower. The Actor also writes one advertiser summary per advertiser; confirm that event on the Store Pricing tab (listed at $0.01 in the Actor's event pricing). This template does not set previousRunDatasetId, so it does not incur change-alert charges; new creatives are detected by comparing the sheet. A default of 3 advertisers × 50 ads is up to about $0.23 in ad charges, plus any summary charges. maxTotalChargeUsd on the Apify node is a hard cap (0.50 in this template). Leave extractAdText off unless you have separately confirmed that option for your use case.

workflows.name: Create daily outreach leads and Gmail drafts from Google Maps with Apify and Sheets
workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow runs every weekday at 6 AM, scrapes Google Maps via Apify to find new businesses for rotating search-and-city pairs, logs them to Google Sheets, and creates Gmail drafts from your own template (never sent) using role-based inboxes discovered from each company’s website.

How it works
Runs on a schedule Monday to Friday at 6 AM (or can be started manually).
Finds an existing Google Sheet by name in Google Drive or creates it with a Leads tab and header row on the first run.
Reads existing leads from Google Sheets, rotates to today’s search and city, and uses Apify’s Google Maps Scraper to fetch up to 20 places.
Filters out closed listings, places without websites, and any company whose website domain already exists in the sheet, keeping up to the configured daily limit.
Uses Apify’s Website Contact Extractor to crawl each website and select a role-based inbox address (for example info@ or hello@) while ignoring personal-looking addresses.
For companies still missing an inbox, runs Apify’s Website Email Scraper and applies the same role-inbox selection rules to fill any remaining gaps.
Appends one row per new company to the Google Sheets Leads tab and creates a Gmail draft for each lead that has an inbox using the configured subject/body template.

Setup
Install the community node @apify/n8n-nodes-apify and add Apify credentials for the Apify nodes.
Add Google Sheets OAuth credentials (used for both Google Sheets and Google Drive/Sheets HTTP requests) so the workflow can find or create the spreadsheet and write to the Leads tab.
Add Gmail credentials and confirm you are comfortable with the workflow creating drafts only (it does not send emails).
Update the Settings values (sheet name, searches, cities, daily lead limit, sender name, and the email subject/body template placeholders) to match your outreach needs.

Requirements
An Apify account, the Google Sheets/Drive and Gmail credentials, and the community node @apify/n8n-nodes-apify. Cost in our tests was about $0.08 per daily run at Apify Store prices (10 new companies); the Maps search costs about $0.02 even on days with no new companies. Each Apify node has a maximum cost per run.

Customization
Edit the Settings node: one search per line, one city per line (one search × city pair per weekday), newPerDay, sender name, and the subject/body with {company}, {city}, {category} and {sender} placeholders. The role-inbox list (info, hello, events, sales, …) is in the inbox-picking Code node.

Additional info
How this differs from existing Google Maps outreach templates: most of them send the email for you (one email per lead, a CSV mailed to you, or an automated sequence). This one never sends: it only creates Gmail drafts you review. It writes only to role inboxes the company publishes on its own website, never to a person's address. It runs daily and incrementally (known domains are skipped, N new per day, rotating searches), needs no AI key, Airtable or CRM, and creates its own Sheet on the first run. Whether you may email a company depends on your country's rules; check before you send.

workflows.name: Find and score LinkedIn buyers at funded accounts with Apify, OpenAI and Slack
workflows.description:
Quick overview
Outbound that starts with timing. Each week this checks your target accounts on Crunchbase, keeps those at the funding stages that buy from you, runs a LinkedIn people search for your buyer title, and has OpenAI score each person and draft an email. Strong fits reach Slack.

How it works
A schedule trigger starts the run every Monday, and a Set node holds your accounts, stages, buyer title and ideal customer.
The first Actor looks each account up on Crunchbase by name or domain: funding rounds, lead investors, headcount, industries and recent news.
A Code node takes the newest real round as the stage, skipping secondary-market sales, and looks for a dated funding headline that names the account.
Accounts outside your stages take the lower path and are logged in a second tab with the reason.
The second Actor runs one LinkedIn people search per remaining account for your buyer title.
A Code node keeps people whose current employer, or else their headline, names the account and ranks them by your title. Accounts with nobody left are logged with the reason.
A Remove Duplicates node skips anyone a previous run already scored.
The Information Extractor returns a fit score, role, reasons, a why-now line, a subject and an email under 90 words.
Every prospect is appended to Google Sheets, and an IF sends the ones at or above your cut-off to Slack.

Setup
Create a free Apify account, copy the API token from Settings, Integrations, and add it as an Apify credential on the two Actor nodes.
Add an OpenAI credential on the chat model node, or swap in any other chat model.
Connect Google Sheets and point the two Sheets nodes at two tabs: one for prospects, one for skipped accounts.
Connect Slack and pick a channel.
Edit the ICP node: your target accounts (domains match best), the funding stages that buy, the buyer title, your ideal customer and what you sell.
Activate the workflow, or run it once by hand first.

Requirements
An Apify account; the free tier covers a weekly run on a few dozen accounts
An OpenAI API key, or any chat model credential n8n supports
Google Sheets and Slack credentials
No Crunchbase API key, LinkedIn login or data-vendor contract

Customization
buyingStages is a plain list, so add Series D or Venture Round if bigger companies buy from you
Set onlyWithFundingNews to true to only contact accounts with a funding headline inside newsWindowDays
strongFitScore decides who reaches Slack without touching the prompt
peoplePerAccount caps how many people per account go to the model
Change buyerTitle and the ideal customer text to use it for recruiting, partnerships or investor research
Wire the optional Salesforce, HubSpot or Gmail node to the Strong fit output to push prospects into your CRM or inbox

Additional info
Do I need a Crunchbase API key? No. The account check reads public Crunchbase company pages through an Actor, so there is no Crunchbase plan or API key. You get funding rounds, lead investors, headcount bands, industries, headquarters and recent news for each account, which is enough venture capital data to decide who is worth a message this week.

How does it decide an account is in a buying window? Crunchbase lists rounds newest first but does not give round dates. So the stage is the newest round that is not a secondary-market sale. Timing comes from a dated funding headline in the account's news, and headlines about tender offers or secondary sales are ignored because they bring in no new money. A headline only counts when it names the account, because a company's news feed often carries other startups' raises.

How do I find people at a specific company on LinkedIn? The LinkedIn people search step searches public LinkedIn profiles by job title and company, with an optional location. It is the same as searching LinkedIn by company, without a login. One search per account returns a page of up to ten people.

Why are some people dropped? A company search matches anyone whose profile mentions the name, current or past. A name that is also a common word pulls in strangers. In testing, one such search returned ten people and none of them worked there. The template keeps a person only when LinkedIn shows the account as their current employer, or when their headline names it. A headline like "Head of Sales, Linear Technology" is rejected for an account called Linear. The sheet's Employer check column says which test passed.

Does LinkedIn have an API for this? LinkedIn's own APIs do not offer a people search to most developers. This template reads public search results instead, so it needs no LinkedIn account and nothing runs under your name.

Will it pitch the same person twice? No. A Remove Duplicates node remembers every profile it has scored, so a weekly run only sends new people to the model and to Slack.

What does it cost? About $0.008 per account checked on Crunchbase, plus about $0.006 for each account that passes and gets a people search. Twenty accounts a week costs well under $0.50 in Apify charges, plus a few small model calls.

What else can these Actors do? Crunchbase Company API returns funding, investors, founders, key people, similar companies and news for up to 100 companies per run, from a Crunchbase URL, a name or a domain. That makes it a quick company enrichment step for any list. LinkedIn People Search API finds people by name, title, company, school or location, and can open each profile for work history when you turn on enrichment. If you self-host n8n, n8n-nodes-crunchbase-company-api wraps the Crunchbase lookup as a community node.

About Apify. LinkedIn People Search API runs on Apify, a platform of ready-made scrapers and APIs for sources that have no usable public API. Actors are pay per use with no subscription, and they run in the cloud, so nothing runs on your machine and nothing breaks when the source changes its markup.

New to Apify? You can set up a free account and get the API token this template needs in a couple of minutes.

workflows.name: Send a weekly competitor LinkedIn digest with Apify, OpenAI and Slack
workflows.description:
Quick overview
Every Monday this reads your competitors' LinkedIn posts and the posts that mention them, and compares each with last week. AI sums up the themes and spots launches, funding or layoffs. Each competitor gets a Google Sheets row. Spikes and announcements alert Slack, and the rest arrive as one digest.

How it works
A Schedule trigger runs every Monday at eight.
A Set node holds your competitors (name, LinkedIn company page, search name), what you sell and the alert rules.
Google Sheets reads last week's row for each competitor, from the same sheet the workflow writes to.
The first Actor reads the past week of posts on each competitor's company page, including the employee posts the page shows.
The second Actor searches public LinkedIn posts that mention each competitor in the same week.
A Code node tags every post with its competitor and drops search results that never name it. Remove Duplicates skips posts that were already counted in an earlier week.
A Code node adds up posts, mentions and engagement per competitor and builds a numbered post list. If nothing could be collected at all, a Slack warning goes out instead.
The Information Extractor writes themes, a two-sentence summary, what changed since last week and one takeaway. It points at any announcement by its post number.
A Code node checks the number against the list and decides between an alert and the digest. Every competitor is appended to Google Sheets.
Alerts go to Slack one by one, with the reason and the post link. The other competitors arrive in one digest message.

Setup
Create a free Apify account, copy the API token from Settings, Integrations, and add it as an Apify credential on both Actor nodes.
Add an OpenAI credential on the chat model node, or swap in any other chat model.
Connect Google Sheets and pick the same spreadsheet and tab on both Sheets nodes.
Connect Slack and pick a channel on all three Slack nodes.
In the Set node, list each competitor's name, LinkedIn company page URL and the name people use for it in posts, and describe what you sell.
Activate the workflow.

Requirements
An Apify account; the free tier covers a weekly run for a handful of competitors
An OpenAI API key, or any chat model credential n8n supports
Google Sheets and Slack credentials
No LinkedIn account, cookie or social listening subscription

Customization
competitors takes a name, a company page URL and a search name each; up to 25 pages and 20 search names per run
search is the phrase looked up in other people's posts. Use the name people actually write, such as "folk CRM" instead of "folk"
spikeFactor, minEngagement and minMentions set what counts as a spike against last week's row
days sets the window; use 1 with a daily schedule for a daily brief
Add your own company to the list to see your posts next to theirs
Add the optional leader posts step, or email the digest instead of posting it

Additional info
How do I monitor competitors on LinkedIn without checking every page? List each competitor's company page once. Every Monday the template reads the past week of posts on each page with a LinkedIn posts API and searches for posts by other people that name them. You get one Slack digest instead of five open tabs, and a separate alert when something actually changed.

What counts as a spike or an announcement? Engagement is likes plus comments on the posts on their page. A competitor alerts when that reaches twice last week's figure and at least 150, when mentions double and reach at least four, or when the model finds a post that announces something new, such as a launch, pricing change, funding, acquisition, partnership, senior hire or layoffs. The model points at the post by its number on a list, and a Code node drops any number that isn't on the list, so an alert always links to a real post.

Is this LinkedIn social listening without a login? Yes. Both Actors read public LinkedIn pages, so you never connect an account or paste a cookie. The mentions step works as a small social listening API for LinkedIn: one row per post with its text, author, date, reactions and comments.

Why are some search results dropped? LinkedIn's post search returns loosely related posts as well as exact matches. The template keeps a result only if the post actually names the competitor. On our test run that dropped one of five results, a post that matched the phrase "folk CRM" without ever saying "folk".

What if LinkedIn hides a competitor's page? Some company feeds aren't shown to signed-out visitors. That competitor is still tracked through the posts that mention it, and the sheet and digest say the page could not be read. If nothing at all can be collected, for example because every URL is wrong, Slack gets a warning instead of an empty digest.

Where does last week's baseline come from? From the same Google Sheet. Each run appends one row per competitor, and the next run reads the latest earlier row back. The first week has nothing to compare with, so only announcements alert that week.

What does it cost? Three competitors cost about 3 cents a week in Apify charges on the free plan and under a cent on a paid plan, plus one small model call per competitor. Search pages seen again within a few days come from a cache and are not charged, and a failed search is never charged.

What else can these Actors do? LinkedIn Posts API returns the recent posts of any public person or company page, or specific posts by URL, with post engagement numbers, tagged companies and top comments. LinkedIn Post Search API finds public posts and articles by keyword, name or hashtag for any date range. If you self-host n8n, n8n-nodes-linkedin-posts-api wraps the posts Actor as a community node.

About Apify. LinkedIn Posts API runs on Apify, a platform of ready-made scrapers and APIs for sources that have no usable public API. Actors are pay per use with no subscription. They run in the cloud, so nothing runs on your machine, and nothing breaks when the source changes its markup.

New to Apify? You can set up a free account and get the API token this template needs in a couple of minutes.

user.name: Francesco Pacifico
user.bio: Software engineer building HTTP-first Apify Actors & ready-to-run n8n automation pipelines for SecOps/TPRM vendor risk, KYB compliance, public procurement, EU healthcare, and judicial auctions.

workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow runs daily to monitor tracked EU EUDAMED UDI-DIs and manufacturer SRNs via Apify, keeps a stateful audit log in an n8n Data Table and Google Sheets, uses OpenAI to triage urgent compliance changes into CAPA guidance, and posts a consolidated alert brief to Slack.

How it works
Runs on a daily schedule (or manually in sample mode) and ensures the n8n Data Table used to store EUDAMED regulatory state exists.
Pulls device and expiring MDR certificate data from the Apify “EU EUDAMED Intelligence” actor based on your UDI-DI and SRN watchlists (or generates built-in sample records for testing).
Compares the latest Apify results with the stored state to detect new entities, recalls/FSCAs, conformity or risk changes, and certificate expiry countdown updates, then upserts the current state to the n8n Data Table.
Appends the detected changes to a Google Sheets tab as an audit ledger.
Selects only items that are new, changed, or due for an expiry reminder and sends up to five of the highest-priority items to OpenAI (gpt-4o-mini) to generate structured MDR/IVDR urgency, article references, impact summaries, and recommended QA actions.
Emails urgent items to a QA/RA address via Gmail and posts a grouped, consolidated regulatory brief to a Slack channel.
After Slack accepts the message, stamps the corresponding entities in the Data Table as notified/reminded, and if Apify or Slack fails it triggers an error workflow to post a failure alert to Slack.

Setup
Create an Apify token in Apify and add an n8n HTTP Header Auth credential that sets Authorization: Bearer , then select it in both Apify HTTP Request steps.
Add credentials for OpenAI, Google Sheets, Gmail, and Slack, and set the Slack channel where the brief and failure alerts should be posted.
Set your Google Sheets document ID and ensure a sheet/tab named EUDAMED_Audit exists for appending the audit log.
Update the watchlist and policy values (UDI-DIs, SRNs, expiry window, reminder days, QA email, and max items) in the configuration step, and optionally test using sampleDay 1 then sampleDay 2 before enabling live Apify calls.
In n8n workflow settings, set this workflow (or a dedicated one) as the error workflow so failures generate the Slack failure alert.

Requirements
n8n 2.48+ with Data Tables enabled (Cloud or self-hosted, core nodes only)
Apify account + API token (francescopacifico1905/eudamed-intelligence Pay-Per-Event)
OpenAI API key, Google Sheets, Gmail, and Slack workspace access

Customization
Adjust remindDaysBefore (90,30,7) or expiringWithinDays in Set UDI-DI Watchlist, SRNs & Alert Policy.
Customize CAPA scoring criteria in AI MDR/IVDR CAPA Triage or raise maxTotalChargeUsd on the Apify nodes for large hospital SKU catalogs.

Additional info
Uses synchronous Pay-Per-Event Apify calls capped at $0.25 per HTTP step; retry-on-fail is intentionally disabled to prevent double billing. Diagnostic NOT_FOUND / INVALID_IDENTIFIER items are never billed by the Actor.

workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow monitors Gmail for new lead replies, uses OpenAI to classify intent and suggest next steps, logs each follow-up to Google Sheets, and emails you alerts, draft replies, and a daily due-today digest.

How it works
Triggers every minute for new Gmail inbox replies (excluding your own mail, promotions/social, and messages already labeled as logged) and also runs each morning on a schedule.
Cleans each new email by extracting sender/subject and the latest reply text, and skips newsletters, automated senders, and empty messages.
Sends the cleaned reply to OpenAI to classify the intent, summarize the message, propose a next step, and extract any follow-up date or referral contact.
Validates the OpenAI output, assigns a priority/status and a due date (or marks the item as “needs review” when confidence is low or parsing fails), then routes actions based on intent.
Emails you immediately for hot leads and “needs review” items, and for questions generates a reply draft and saves it to Gmail without sending.
Appends every processed reply as a new row in a Google Sheets “Follow-ups” tab and then applies a Gmail label to the original message so it is not processed twice.
Each morning, reads the Google Sheet for open or “needs review” follow-ups due today or overdue and emails you a prioritized list.

Setup
Connect Gmail credentials with permission to read messages, create drafts, send notification emails, and manage labels.
Add an OpenAI credential and select a compatible chat model in the OpenAI steps.
Connect Google Sheets credentials and create a spreadsheet with a tab named “Follow-ups” containing the required header columns used by the append step.
In Gmail, create a label that matches the configured label name (default: “Follow-up logged”).
Update the Settings values, including your Google Sheet URL, alert email address, name, business context, timezone, and any thresholds like min_confidence and not_now_days.

user.name: Oriol
user.bio: Developer and founder of Grenetic. I build practical n8n automations with AI for small businesses: simple to set up, free to run and easy to adapt. Need something custom? Get in touch through my website.

workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow collects a source URL or text via an n8n Form, uses Google Gemini to generate LinkedIn, Instagram, and X draft posts plus an image idea in your brand voice, and appends the drafts to a Google Sheets spreadsheet.

How it works
Receives a submission from an n8n Form with a Source URL and/or some idea text.
If a URL is provided, it fetches the web page via HTTP and extracts the title and paragraph text from the HTML.
Falls back to the submitted idea text when no URL is provided or when the page fetch fails, then checks that there is usable source text.
If source text exists, sends the source, brand settings, and writing rules to Google Gemini to generate LinkedIn, Instagram, and X drafts plus an image idea.
Parses the model response into structured fields and formats them into a single row with a Draft status.
If no usable text is available, creates a row indicating the page could not be read and asks you to paste text in the form.
Appends the resulting row to Google Sheets for review and manual publishing.

Setup
Add a Google Gemini API credential and select the Gemini model used for generating the posts.
Connect Google Sheets credentials, then select the target spreadsheet and sheet in the Google Sheets append step.
Use an empty sheet (n8n creates the headers on the first run) or one with these exact headers: Date, Source, LinkedIn, Instagram, X, Image idea, Status.
Update the Brand settings values (brand name, description, audience, voice, language, and call to action) to match your business.
Execute the workflow once and use the generated form URL to submit a Source URL and/or idea text.

Requirements
An n8n instance (cloud or self-hosted)
A Google Gemini API key (the free tier is enough)
A Google account with access to Google Sheets

Customization
Change the Brand settings values to match your brand, audience, tone, language and call to action
Edit the writing rules in the Write the posts step to change length, style or hashtags
Swap the Gemini model for any other chat model supported by n8n
Add or remove social networks by updating the output parser and the Prepare row step
Replace the form trigger with a schedule or RSS trigger to generate drafts automatically

workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow collects a campaign image and brand brief via an n8n Form, validates the upload, and uses Google Gemini Vision to score brand and platform fit, then returns an HTML QA report, with optional logging to Google Sheets and optional notification via Gmail.

How it works
Receives a creative asset upload and campaign/brand requirements through an n8n Form.
Validates the file type, size, and required brief fields and stops before any AI call if the upload is invalid.
Sends the image and brief to Google Gemini Vision and asks for a structured JSON review covering detected text, platform fit, brand alignment, hierarchy, accessibility, issues, and suggested edits.
Parses and validates Gemini’s JSON response, then assigns a status (PASS, MANUAL REVIEW, or NEEDS CHANGES) based on critical issues and score thresholds.
Displays an HTML QA report back to the submitter in the form completion page.
If enabled, appends the review results to a Google Sheets tab named Reviews.
If enabled and a fixed reviewer email is configured, sends the HTML report to the reviewer via Gmail, and captures any optional-action errors for manual follow-up.

Setup
Add a Google Gemini API credential and select an image-capable Gemini model in the Google Gemini node.
Review and adjust the pass/manual-review score thresholds, max upload size, and fixed reviewer email in the workflow settings values.
To enable logging, connect Google Sheets, set the target spreadsheet ID, and create a Reviews sheet with the expected columns used by the append step.
To enable email notifications, connect a Gmail account and replace the default reviewer email with a real address, then turn on notifications.
Copy the n8n Form URL for “Creative Asset Intake” and share it with your team (and add n8n authentication or IP allowlisting if you want to restrict access).

workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow uses Google Sheets, Google Calendar, and Supergreen (WhatsApp) to send interactive appointment reminder polls, capture client poll votes in real time, update booking status in the sheet, and notify staff when clients are running late or request a reschedule.

How it works
Runs every hour to scan upcoming appointments.
Reads rows from the Google Sheets “Appointments” tab and filters to scheduled bookings within the reminder window that have not been sent a reminder yet.
Checks the corresponding Google Calendar event (when an event ID is present) and skips messaging if the event is cancelled while updating the sheet to reflect the cancellation.
Sends a 3-option WhatsApp poll via Supergreen to let the client confirm, report running late, or request a reschedule.
Updates Google Sheets to mark the reminder as sent with a timestamp.
Triggers when Supergreen receives an incoming WhatsApp poll vote, matches the voter to the nearest active booking in Google Sheets, and maps the vote to a new booking status.
Updates the booking status in Google Sheets, replies to the client on WhatsApp (including a reschedule link when requested), and sends a WhatsApp message to a staff group for “Running Late” or “Reschedule Requested” votes.

Setup
Install and configure the community node n8n-nodes-supergreen and add a Supergreen API credential for WhatsApp messaging and webhooks.
Add Google Sheets OAuth2 credentials, create an “Appointments” sheet with the expected columns (including bookingId, phone, appointmentIso, calendarEventId, status, reminderSent, reminderSentAt, lastVoteAt), and set your spreadsheet ID in both configuration steps.
Add Google Calendar OAuth2 credentials and set the calendar ID used to validate events (and ensure appointment rows contain calendarEventId when you want calendar cross-checking).
Set your business name, reminder window (hours), client reschedule URL, and the staff WhatsApp group chat ID used for alerts.

Requirements
n8n-nodes-supergreen (tested v0.1.5 — verified community node available directly on n8n Cloud and self-hosted n8n) + Supergreen API account (https://supergreen.cc)

Customization
Change reminderWindowHours (e.g., 48h or 2h), customize the 3 WhatsApp poll choices, or route staff alerts to Slack or Telegram instead of a WhatsApp group.

workflows.description:
Quick overview
List products with a photo link in a Google Sheet; for each, GenMagic suggests three camera moves by email, you reply with the ones to make, and Seedance 1.5 Pro animates the real photo for each pick. Clips go to Google Drive and the row gets links and cost.

How it works
Check Every Hour starts a run and Set Video Settings holds the video shape (9:16 by default), the length and how many camera moves to suggest.
Read New Products in Sheets reads the rows whose Status is new and Limit to Next Product takes the first one.
Write Camera Moves asks a GenMagic text model for three different moves (an orbit, a push-in, a turntable spin, a light sweep) that never change the product's shape, colour or label, and Format Moves for Review checks the photo link and numbers them.
Ask Which Moves by Email emails the list and waits; Read Picked Moves takes the numbers you reply, and If Any Move Picked sends a 0 to Mark Product Skipped in Sheets.
Split Picked Moves makes one item per pick and Animate Product Photo renders each with Seedance 1.5 Pro at 720p with your photo as the opening frame, so the product stays exactly as photographed.
Save Video to Drive stores each clip, Collect Clip Links lists the links (or a failed clip's reason) and the cost, and Mark Product Done in Sheets writes them and the status to the row.

Setup
Install the GenMagic node: open the nodes panel, search for GenMagic and install it from More from the community (on self-hosted n8n you can also install the package n8n-nodes-genmagic under Settings, Community Nodes).
Create a free GenMagic account and an API key at https://genmagic.co/get-api-key?utm_source=n8n&utm_medium=template&utm_campaign=product-photo-video and choose it as the GenMagic API credential on Write Camera Moves and Animate Product Photo.
Create a Google Sheet with the columns Product, Photo URL, Style, Status, Video, Cost (USD), add rows with a public https photo link and Status new, and select it in Read New Products in Sheets, Mark Product Done in Sheets and Mark Product Skipped in Sheets.
Connect Gmail in Ask Which Moves by Email with your address in Send To, and Google Drive in Save Video to Drive, then activate the workflow.

Requirements
n8n (Cloud or self-hosted) with the verified GenMagic community node installed
A GenMagic account and API key; new verified accounts get free starter credit, and at today's prices each 5-second 720p clip costs about 20 cents
A Google account for Gmail, Google Sheets and Google Drive, and product photos reachable by a public https link

Customization
Use Kling 3.0 or Veo 3.1 in Animate Product Photo for richer motion, or turn on sound
Set aspect_ratio to 1:1 for marketplace listings or 16:9 for a website hero, and seconds up to 12
Approve through Slack or Telegram instead of Gmail, which can also wait for a reply

user.name: Cap.Guru
user.bio: Captcha solving API for automation and AI agents: reCAPTCHA, Cloudflare Turnstile, hCaptcha, GeeTest, FunCaptcha and text captchas. Ready-to-use n8n workflows, an MCP server and Python and Node.js modules.

workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow takes a captcha image URL or Base64 payload, submits it to the Cap.Guru API for text recognition, polls for the result, and returns the solved text (optionally evaluating arithmetic captchas).

How it works
Starts manually or is called from another workflow with imageUrl or imageBase64 (and optional vernet).
Validates inputs and, if only a URL is provided, downloads the image and converts it to a Base64 string.
Sends the Base64 image to Cap.Guru (in.php) to create a recognition task.
Waits 5 seconds and polls Cap.Guru (res.php) repeatedly until a result is ready or a 2-minute timeout is reached.
If the recognized text is an arithmetic expression, calculates the numeric answer.
Outputs the solved text (plus expression when applicable) along with the Cap.Guru taskId.

Setup
Create a Cap.Guru account and API key.
In n8n, create an HTTP Query Auth credential that sends your API key as a query parameter named key, and select it in both Cap.Guru HTTP Request steps.
Provide an imageUrl or imageBase64 when running the workflow (optionally set vernet, such as 22 for arithmetic captchas).

Requirements
A Cap.Guru account with an API key and a positive balance (get one at cap.guru)

Customization
Pass vernet for a specific captcha kind (22 for arithmetic), or change the API address to https://api.cap.guru from Russia

Additional info
Use the answer right away: many sites show a new captcha on every page load. Case usually does not matter, so k7m4p and K7M4P are both correct. Docs: https://docs.cap.guru/en/apiclick/text.html

workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow runs daily, reads unchecked slogans from Google Sheets, searches live USPTO trademark records via an Apify actor, and writes a risk verdict plus matching owner and serial number back to the sheet.

How it works
Runs every day at 9:00 AM on a schedule trigger.
Reads rows from a Google Sheets tab named “Slogans” where the “Verdict” column is empty.
Processes each slogan one at a time and runs Magnova’s “USPTO Trademark Search” Apify actor to fetch up to 10 LIVE trademark records for the phrase.
Compares the returned marks against the slogan and assigns a verdict of “RISK — live trademark match” for an exact match in IC 016/021/024/025, “CHECK — similar live mark” for phrase-containing matches in those classes, or “No live match found” otherwise.
Updates the same Google Sheets row by matching on the “Slogan” column and writing the verdict, owner, and serial number.

Setup
Create or choose a Google Sheet with columns Slogan, Verdict, Owner, and Serial (in a tab named “Slogans”) and add your Google Sheets credentials in n8n.
Paste your Google Sheets document URL/ID into the Google Sheets nodes and confirm the correct sheet/tab is selected.
Add your Apify API token credentials and ensure the workflow can run the actor ID I8KvtBliDeyVghVzU.
(Optional) Adjust the schedule time, Apify maxResults, or maxTotalChargeUsd limit to fit your usage and cost controls.
